references.text: The Lord promises to dwell among the children of Israel and be their God, which corresponds to 'the Lord his God is with him'.
The Lord turned Balaam's curse into a blessing because he loved Israel, showing that God does not see sin in Jacob.
Blessed is the one whose transgressions are forgiven and whose sins are covered, reflecting that God does not see wrongdoing in Jacob.
Blessed is the people who know the joyful shout (teruah) and walk in the light of the Lord's presence - a direct parallel to 'the king's joyous cry is with him'.
The Lord, the God of hosts, is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress - parallel to 'the Lord his God is with him'.
The Lord removes Israel's transgressions like a cloud, which corresponds to his not seeing wrongdoing in Jacob.
In those days Israel's guilt will be sought but not found - parallel to God not seeing sin in Jacob.
The Lord your king goes before you; the Lord is at their head - parallel to 'the king's joyous cry is with him'.
The Lord is king in the midst of Israel; they shall no longer fear - parallel to God's presence as king among the people.
Paul quotes Psalm 32 that blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven and whose sins are covered, reflecting that God does not see wrongdoing in Jacob.
If God is for us, who can be against us? - expresses the same truth as 'the Lord his God is with him'.
